back: A group of businesses or people producing the same kind of goods or services.
Industry that extracts natural resources: farming, mining, fishing, forestry.
Industry that processes raw materials into goods, or builds: manufacturing, processing, construction.
Industry that provides services: trade, transport, banking, tourism, education, health.

front: Name four indigenous industries of Zimbabwe.
back: Iron smelting and blacksmithing, pottery, weaving and basketry, mining (also carving, salt making, leatherwork).

front: What were indigenous iron furnaces fuelled with?
back: Charcoal, with air pumped in by bellows.

front: Why did some indigenous industries decline in the colonial period?
back: Cheap imported and factory goods replaced local products; people left for wage work; skills were taught less often.

front: How are the three types of industry linked?
back: Primary industry supplies raw materials to secondary industry, whose goods are moved, financed and sold by tertiary industry.

front: Give three reasons why industry is important.
back: It creates jobs, earns foreign currency through exports and pays taxes (also adds value and preserves heritage).
